haiku-low.q1: It saves the order as PENDING and an OrderPlaced outbox event in one transaction. The customer gets 202 Accepted with the orderId immediately.
haiku-low.q2: Only after the broker confirms it has the event, when the relay marks the row SENT. If it crashes after confirmation but before marking, the row is resent on the next poll.
haiku-low.q3: Each event is published with orderId as its key. The broker delivers events with the same key in the order they were published.
haiku-low.q4: Payment acts only on an InventoryReserved event and writes its PENDING_CHARGE row only after it arrives. So it never charges for stock not held.
haiku-low.q5: Each writes results to its own outbox, and its relay publishes them. Publishing straight after commit is rejected because a crash there would lose the event; the saved outbox row is sent later.
haiku-low.q6: Each consumer checks a processed_events table keyed by eventId in the same transaction as its state change. If found, it acknowledges and skips. A unique orderId key is a backup.
haiku-low.q7: Payment saves the key charge:orderId before calling the provider. The redelivered message reuses that key, so the provider returns the first result without charging again.
haiku-low.q8: A decline is a normal answer that leads to PaymentDeclined. A timeout or 5xx is an error that goes to the retry policy.
haiku-low.q9: PaymentDeclined triggers the release. Inventory releases the reservation from RESERVED to RELEASED, doing nothing if none exists.
haiku-low.q10: It consumes PaymentCaptured, PaymentDeclined and InventoryRejected. It changes status only from PENDING, writing CONFIRMED or CANCELLED plus the final event.
haiku-low.q11: Only OrderConfirmed and OrderCancelled events trigger email. If sending fails, Notification records FAILED and acknowledges without retry or paging; the order status is unchanged.
haiku-low.q12: Four attempts total, with waits of 1 s, 10 s and 60 s between them. Then the message goes to the consumer's DLQ, on-call is paged, and the order keeps its current status.

sonnet.q1: It saves the order as PENDING and writes the OrderPlaced event to the outbox, both in one transaction. The customer gets 202 Accepted with the orderId.
sonnet.q2: The relay marks a row SENT only after the broker confirms it has the event. If it crashes after the confirm but before marking, the row is sent again on the next poll, so delivery is at-least-once (duplicates possible, no loss).
sonnet.q3: Every event is published with orderId as its key, and the broker delivers events with the same key in publish order. In-place retries (blocking later messages) and relays stopping at a failed publish also preserve this order.
sonnet.q4: Payment acts only on the InventoryReserved event, and writes its PENDING_CHARGE row only after that event arrives. If stock is rejected, Payment is never called, so no card is charged without reserved stock.
sonnet.q5: Each has its own outbox and relay. The service writes its state change and the event to the outbox in one transaction, and the relay publishes it. If it crashes after commit, the event is still in the outbox and gets published later, so it is not lost. No service publishes directly after commit.
sonnet.q6: It checks processed_events for the eventId, written in the same transaction as the state change. If already present, it acknowledges and skips. A unique key on orderId (one reservation and one payment row per order) is a second guard.
sonnet.q7: The idempotency key charge:orderId, saved on the payment row before the provider call. The redelivered message calls the provider with the same key, the provider returns the first result without charging again, and Payment records that result.
sonnet.q8: A decline is a normal answer: Payment records DECLINED and publishes PaymentDeclined, which leads to order cancellation and stock release. A timeout or 5xx is an error that goes to the retry policy (retries with the same key, then DLQ and page if all fail).
sonnet.q9: The PaymentDeclined event triggers it, and the Inventory service releases the reservation (RESERVED to RELEASED, no event published; does nothing if there was no reservation).
sonnet.q10: Order Service has its own consumer group and consumes PaymentCaptured, PaymentDeclined and InventoryRejected. It changes status only from PENDING (other transitions ignored and logged). In one transaction it sets CONFIRMED or CANCELLED, records the eventId, and writes OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled to the outbox.
sonnet.q11: Only the OrderConfirmed and OrderCancelled events trigger the email. If sending fails, Notification records FAILED, acknowledges, does not retry or page, and the order status is unchanged.
sonnet.q12: Four attempts in total (initial plus retries after waits of 1 s, 10 s and 60 s). Then the message goes to that consumer's DLQ, on-call is paged, and the consumer moves on. Nothing is rolled back: the order stays PENDING, reservation stays RESERVED, payment row stays PENDING_CHARGE (in the Payment example).
